verdict.rationale: Claude Code keeps its automation definitions (settings, skills, subagents, and hooks) as files in the project's .claude directory. The docs explicitly direct users to commit these to git, so they can be versioned and shared. Review and rollback, however, come from git rather than any native Claude history or rollback feature, and Cowork scheduled tasks show no versioning at all. missing for 10: native version history for automations, a built-in review or diff workflow, documented rollback, versioning for Cowork scheduled tasks, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Commit project files to git to share them with your team; files in ~/.claude are personal configuration that applies across all your projects.
Hooks are user-defined shell commands. Claude Code runs them at specific points in its lifecycle
